chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: The gangster atmosphere in Hampton's band that drove him out
summary: Cobb describes Curly Hamner, the masseur and the valet carrying a pistol for Hampton, cursing in front of wives, and says it broke up a good band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I stopped mine coming around with that (inaudible).

Well, you had the Curly Hamilton, you had the masseur, Harrison, and you had the valey, Leroy, and they were the cream of the crop as far as Hamp. Hamp had a permit to carry a pistol, and Leroy carried it for him, you know, and they all had their thing going, (inaudible) and it just got to be a gangster band instead of friendly, and that was too much for me, and I didn't want any more of it.
I really didn't, because you can't play happy under these circumstances.

And I tell you, I'll be a man to tell him now, and he knew what went on. He knows better than anybody else, because he let it happen, and that's my boss man. He's [sharp], he's everything, you know. This knocks him out. That's what he likes, God bless him. (Inaudible), politician. This what you want, good. But under the circumstances, I'm a timid young man, and I want to play with my heart, and I was scared to death somebody going to do something wrong to me, and that's what it was getting to.

But I tell you one thing, it broke up a darn good band, because guys started to leaving one by one. (inaudible). I don't know if he really knew what happened. I don't know if Gladys knew what happened, but I knew what happened, and I

wasn't going no further myself. I didn't want my wife exposed to this sort of thing, that I couldn't bring her around under a peaceful situation wherever I'm working. I was able to do it prior to that, but I couldn't do it then.
